draft.title: Radius, diameter, circumference and pi
card: Radius
the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge.
Diameter
the distance straight across a circle through the centre. It is twice the radius.
Circumference
the distance around the circle. For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter is the same number, called pi (π), about 3.14.
So circumference ≈ 3.14 × diameter. Example: a circle with diameter 10 cm has circumference about 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm.
draft.remember: Diameter is twice the radius. Circumference is about 3.14 times the diameter.

a.q: A circle has a radius of 7 cm. What is its diameter?
a.why: The diameter is twice the radius, so 2 × 7 = 14 cm. Halving the radius gives 3.5 cm, which mixes up the two.
a.clue: The diameter goes all the way across.

b.q: A round pond has a radius of 5 m. About how far is it around the edge? Use π ≈ 3.14.
b.why: Diameter = 2 × 5 = 10 m, so circumference ≈ 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 m. Using the radius directly gives 15.7 m, which is only half the distance.
